mainTopic: When sacred meat in a mixture can be nullified (בטל), and whether רבי יוחנן holds תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא
overview: This amud continues the discussion of a ברייתא about a piece of חטאת meat mixed into one hundred other pieces. ריש לקיש explained that the ברייתא allows nullification only when the piece was crushed. The גמרא first explains that רבי יהודה disagrees because of his rule מין במינו לא בטיל. It then asks why the ברייתא switched to a case of חולין, and answers that the תנא preferred to teach a pure-in-pure case. Next it asks why the first clause allows nullification and the second does not. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי answers that the first clause is only a rabbinic impurity of liquids, while the second clause involves a Torah prohibition. רבה's answer (לאו versus כרת) is left as a קשיא, and רב אשי's answer (דבר שיש לו מתירין) is rejected as a mistake. Finally, the גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן really holds that תרומה nowadays is from the Torah, given his lenient view in the two-baskets ברייתא. It answers that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה disagrees: same kind is never nullified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא. He follows his own known rule that a food mixed with its own kind cannot be nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his usual reasoning, because he says: a food mixed with its own kind is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רבי יהודה does not allow nullification even when the piece is crushed. He is simply following a rule he holds everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if crushing removes the special importance of the piece, רבי יהודה has a separate reason to forbid it. Here sacred meat was mixed with sacred meat, so it is מין במינו. For him, a same-kind mixture is never nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with a view he holds elsewhere
A food mixed with its own kind
Is nullified, loses its identity in the majority

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
as he said: a type mixed with its own type is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an earlier question from before this section about why רבי יהודה disagrees in the ברייתא as ריש לקיש explains it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the opinion to a consistent independent principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי יהודה should agree that a crushed piece is nullified.
steps.terutzMaskana: He disagrees because of his general rule, מין במינו לא בטיל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a same-kind mixture is never nullified.

steps.title: Why didn't the ברייתא contrast crushed and uncrushed pieces?
steps.stepSummary: If an uncrushed piece is not nullified, the ברייתא could have taught that difference inside the first case. Instead it switched to a new case of pure חטאת mixed with חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the piece was not crushed, what is the law? It is not nullified. Then instead of teaching: 'But a piece of pure חטאת that got mixed into one hundred pieces of pure חולין is not nullified,' the ברייתא should have drawn the line within the same case: 'When does this apply? When the piece was crushed. But if it was not crushed, it is not nullified!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's reading. It asks why the ברייתא chose a different case when it had an easier distinction available in the very same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says nullification works only for a crushed piece, so an uncrushed piece is not nullified. That gives a ready-made contrast inside the first case. The גמרא asks why the תנא skipped it and brought a case of חולין instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushed or broken into small parts
It is not nullified (literally: it does not 'go up' or get absorbed)
Instead of teaching
Let him draw the distinction and teach it within the same case
When does this apply? (introduces a limitation)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying an uncrushed piece is nullified. According to ריש לקיש's reading, an uncrushed piece is not nullified. The question is only about how the ברייתא chose to word its contrast.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא נִימּוֹחָה מַאי — לֹא תַּעֲלֶה,
phrases.english: But if it was not crushed, what? It is not nullified.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּתָנֵי: אֲבָל חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל חַטָּאת טְהוֹרָה
phrases.english: Instead of teaching: but a piece of pure sin-offering

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבָה בְּמֵאָה חֲתִיכוֹת שֶׁל חוּלִּין טְהוֹרוֹת
phrases.english: that got mixed into one hundred pieces of pure non-sacred meat
is not nullified,
let him distinguish and teach it within the same case:
When is this said? When it was crushed,
but if it was not crushed, it is not nullified!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לֹא נִימּוֹחָה מַאי — לֹא תַּעֲלֶה, אַדְּתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues testing ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא, now from the angle of how the ברייתא is structured.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the ברייתא refers only to a crushed piece
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If crushed versus uncrushed is the key difference, the ברייתא should have taught that contrast directly instead of switching to a case with חולין.

steps.title: The תנא preferred to teach a pure-in-pure case
steps.stepSummary: The תנא chose the case of pure meat mixed with pure meat because it teaches a new point.
steps.simpleTranslation: He prefers to teach pure pieces mixed with pure pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the תנא had a reason to pick the חולין case, because he wanted to teach about pure meat mixed with pure meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא could have contrasted crushed and uncrushed pieces. He chose instead to teach that even when no impurity is involved, a pure חטאת piece in pure חולין is not nullified. That new lesson was worth more to him than the simpler contrast.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure items mixed with pure items
He prefers it, it is better in his eyes

phrases.english: Pure pieces mixed with pure pieces are preferable to him.
phrases.notes: He means the תנא wanted to teach this case because it has its own new lesson.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the תנא's choice of case as teaching a separate new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The switch to a חולין case looked unnecessary under ריש לקיש's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא deliberately taught the pure-in-pure case for its own lesson, so ריש לקיש's reading stands.

steps.title: According to ריש לקיש, why do the two clauses differ?
steps.stepSummary: If both clauses deal with a crushed piece, why is it nullified in the first clause but not in the second?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to ריש לקיש, what is different about the first clause, and what is different about the last clause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on ריש לקיש. If crushing is what allows nullification, why does crushing help in the first clause but not in the second?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריש לקיש, both clauses speak of a crushed piece. The first clause (impure חטאת in pure pieces) allows nullification, but the second (pure חטאת in pure חולין) does not. The גמרא wants to know what reason accounts for the different result.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
The first clause of a ברייתא or משנה
The last clause of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And according to Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא?
phrases.english: what is different about the first clause, and what is different about the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to ריש לקיש's reading, about the logic of the ruling rather than its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's explanation that both clauses deal with a crushed piece
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the crushed state is the same in both clauses, the different outcomes need a reason; otherwise the reading seems inconsistent.

steps.title: רב שישא: rabbinic impurity versus a Torah prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי explains the difference between the clauses. The first clause involves impurity from liquids, which is only דרבנן, so nullification is allowed. The second clause involves a prohibition מדאורייתא, so it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: The first clause deals with impurity of liquids, which is rabbinic. The last clause deals with a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא answers the question of step 4. The two clauses differ because the prohibition in each one has a different level of strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, the חטאת became impure through liquids, and that impurity is only דרבנן, so the רבנן were lenient and allowed it to be nullified. In the second clause, sacred meat is forbidden to non-כהנים מדאורייתא, so it cannot be nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity passed on through liquids
A rule from the Sages, not from the Torah itself
A rule from the Torah itself

steps.whatToRemember: Under ריש לקיש, the ברייתא allows nullification only for a crushed piece. Even then, it works only where the problem is דרבנן (impurity of liquids). Where the problem is מדאורייתא (sacred meat mixed with חולין), the piece is not nullified.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: the רבנן may be lenient about nullification when the prohibition is only rabbinic, but not when it comes from the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
The first clause deals with impurity of liquids, which is rabbinic.
The last clause deals with a Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: רֵישָׁא, בְּטוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two clauses by the level of the prohibition (rabbinic versus Torah)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses deal with a crushed piece, so they seemed to need the same outcome.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause's impurity is only דרבנן, so it can be nullified; the second clause's prohibition is מדאורייתא, so it cannot.

steps.title: What if the impurity came from a creeping animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out what follows from רב שישא's answer: if the meat became impure from a שרץ, which is מדאורייתא, it would not be nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the impurity came from a שרץ, what would the law be? It would not be nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick question and answers it right away. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שישא said the first case is nullified only because impurity from liquids is דרבנן. So the גמרא concludes that impurity from a שרץ, which is מדאורייתא, would not be nullified. The next step uses this result to attack the way the ברייתא is written.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from touching a dead creeping animal, which is impurity מדאורייתא
It is not nullified (literally, 'it does not go up')

phrases.english: But impurity from a creeping animal, what would the law be?
phrases.notes: He means: what if the piece of meat in the first case had become impure by touching a שרץ instead of liquids?

phrases.english: It would not be nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what follows from רב שישא's answer in step 5, to prepare a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What would the law be if the sacred meat were made impure by a שרץ, which is impurity מדאורייתא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It would not be nullified, because the reason for nullification (impurity that is only דרבנן) is missing.

steps.title: The ברייתא should have taught the contrast inside its first case
steps.stepSummary: If impurity from a שרץ is not nullified, the ברייתא could have taught that contrast within the first case instead of switching to a piece of חטאת mixed with חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead of teaching in the latter clause, 'But a piece of a pure חטאת that became mixed with one hundred pieces of pure חולין is not nullified,' let it make the distinction within the same case: 'When is this said? With impurity from liquids. But with impurity from a שרץ, it is not nullified!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב שישא's answer. If there really is a difference between liquid impurity and שרץ impurity, why didn't the ברייתא just say so in the first case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנא usually shows a contrast in the simplest way, inside the same case. The ברייתא instead switched to a completely new case (חטאת mixed with חולין). That suggests the difference between the clauses is not about liquids versus שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching
Let it make a distinction and teach it within the same case
In what case are these words said? (a phrase used to limit a ruling)
Impurity that comes from liquids, which is only דרבנן

steps.confusionAlert: This question sounds almost the same as step 2. There it was aimed at ריש לקיש's crushed-versus-uncrushed reading; here it is aimed at רב שישא's liquids-versus-שרץ explanation. It is the same kind of question, aimed at a different claim, and step 8 answers it the same way step 3 did.

phrases.english: Instead of teaching in the latter clause:
But a piece of a ritually pure sin-offering
that became mixed with one hundred pieces
of ritually pure non-sacred meat is not nullified,
let it make a distinction and teach it within the same case:
phrases.notes: 'The same case' means the first case, impure sacred meat mixed with pure sacred meat.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
With impurity from liquids,
but with impurity from a creeping animal, it is not nullified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 6 to challenge how the ברייתא is written.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי's explanation that the first clause deals with impurity from liquids.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If liquid impurity and שרץ impurity are treated differently, the clearest way to teach that is a contrast within the first case. Switching to a new case of חטאת and חולין makes the explanation look unlikely.

steps.title: The תנא preferred the case of pure mixed with pure
steps.stepSummary: The תנא chose the new case on purpose, because a pure piece mixed with pure pieces teaches something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pure piece mixed with pure pieces is preferable to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא switched cases because the תנא wanted to teach the more surprising case of pure meat mixed with pure meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the ברייתא could have taught the liquids-versus-שרץ contrast, a case where nothing is impure at all adds something new. You might think a mix of only pure pieces is no problem, so it is a bigger lesson that it still is not nullified. This is the same answer the גמרא gave in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: A pure piece mixed with pure pieces
He prefers it; it is better for him to teach

phrases.english: A pure piece mixed with pure pieces is preferable to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the תנא of the ברייתא. This is the same answer the גמרא gave in step 3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and keeps רב שישא's explanation standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the תנא chose that case: it teaches more.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The switch to a new case shows that the liquids-versus-שרץ explanation is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The switch was a teaching choice, so רב שישא's explanation can still stand.

steps.title: רבה: the first clause is a לאו, the second is כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a different explanation of the two clauses. The first clause involves only a simple prohibition (לאו), so nullification works. The second involves a כרת prohibition, so it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The first clause involves a standard prohibition; the latter clause involves a prohibition punishable by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a new way to explain why the first case is nullified and the second is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה does not rely on the difference between דרבנן and דאורייתא. He points to how serious the prohibition is. In the first case, eating impure sacred meat is a plain לאו. In the second case, a non-כהן eating pure קדשים is a כרת prohibition, which he treats as too serious to be nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause
The latter clause
A standard Torah prohibition, without כרת
A Torah prohibition whose punishment is כרת (being cut off)

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The first clause involves a standard prohibition,
the latter clause involves a prohibition punishable by karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 4, instead of רב שישא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the difference between the clauses by how serious each prohibition is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses deal with a crushed piece, so they should have the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: A לאו can be nullified, but a כרת prohibition cannot, so the two clauses differ.

steps.title: רבה contradicts his own rule, and the difficulty stays
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבה himself taught that for any Torah prohibition, לאו and כרת are treated the same for nullification. The גמרא leaves this as an unanswered difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it רבה himself who said: For anything forbidden by the Torah, there is no difference between a standard prohibition and a כרת prohibition! This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's answer using his own words from elsewhere, and ends with 'קשיא', meaning the question is not answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer depends on treating לאו and כרת differently. But רבה himself said that for all Torah prohibitions, the seriousness of the punishment makes no difference to nullification. Because of this contradiction, the גמרא does not accept רבה's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a contradiction)
In matters that are forbidden by the Torah
There is no difference
It is difficult: the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers were given for why the clauses differ. רב שישא's answer (דרבנן impurity from liquids versus a Torah prohibition) survives. רבה's answer (לאו versus כרת) is left as a 'קשיא', because it clashes with his own rule that all Torah prohibitions are treated alike.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end is not a new question. It means the challenge just raised stays unanswered. It does not prove רבה wrong for good, but his explanation is left weak.

phrases.english: But wasn't it Rabba himself who said:
With anything forbidden by Torah law,
there is no difference between a standard prohibition
and a prohibition punishable by karet!
phrases.notes: He means both are treated the same when it comes to being nullified in a mixture.

phrases.english: This is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer from step 9 using his own ruling, and closes that line unresolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that a לאו is nullified but a כרת prohibition is not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה elsewhere rules that all Torah prohibitions are treated the same for nullification, whether לאו or כרת. So he cannot explain the difference between the clauses by that distinction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction is not resolved ('קשיא'), so רבה's explanation is left weak.

steps.title: רב אשי: the sacred meat has a way to become permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the second clause is stricter because the piece of sacred meat is a דבר שיש לו מתירין, and such an item is never nullified, even in a thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In the second clause, the meat is not nullified because it is something that has a way to become permitted. Anything like that is not nullified, even in a mixture of a thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a third way to explain why the first clause allows nullification and the second clause does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's approach (לאו versus כרת) was just knocked down. רב אשי gives a completely different reason. The sacred meat is not totally forbidden, because it is permitted to someone. An item like that never gets nullified, no matter how large the mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a teaching
An item that has a way to become permitted, so its prohibition is not permanent
Becomes nullified in a larger mixture
Even in a thousand, meaning no ratio is ever enough

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The latter clause is different because it is
an item that has a way to become permitted,
and any item that has a way to become permitted
is not nullified, even in a thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: סֵיפָא — מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי לֵיהּ דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה's answer was left unresolved, רב אשי gives a new answer to the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New legal principle distinguishing the two clauses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between the clauses depended on the type of prohibition (לאו or כרת).
steps.terutzMaskana: The second clause is not nullified because the meat is a דבר שיש לו מתירין.

steps.title: רב אשי's explanation is rejected as a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the rule of דבר שיש לו מתירין does not fit here. For a כהן the meat was always permitted, and for a ישראל it will always be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of רב אשי is a mistake. Permitted for whom? If for a כהן, it is fully permitted to him anyway. If for a ישראל, it is forbidden to him forever! So this statement of רב אשי is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's explanation and calls it a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דבר שיש לו מתירין is something forbidden now that will become permitted to the same person later. Here nothing like that happens. A כהן could eat the meat even before the mix, and a ישראל can never eat it. So the principle simply does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, a statement that has no basis
For whom?
It is fully permitted
It is forbidden forever

steps.whatToRemember: The principle of דבר שיש לו מתירין only works when the same person will later be allowed the item. If it is always permitted to one group and never to another, the principle does not apply.

phrases.english: And this statement of Rav Ashi is a mistake.
Permitted for whom?
If for a priest, it is fully permitted to him anyway.
If for an Israelite, it is forbidden to him forever!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא דְּרַב אָשֵׁי בְּדוּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Rather, this statement of Rav Ashi is a mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the answer given in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects רב אשי's explanation of the second clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no person for whom the meat goes from forbidden to permitted, so it is not a דבר שיש לו מתירין.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן hold תרומה today is from the Torah? The two-baskets case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן holds that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא. It quotes a ברייתא: when two סאה measures, one of חולין and one of תרומה, fell into two baskets, one of חולין and one of תרומה, everything is permitted. We assume each fell into its own kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוחנן really hold that תרומה nowadays is from the Torah? But a ברייתא teaches: There were two baskets, one of חולין and one of תרומה. In front of them were two סאה measures, one of חולין and one of תרומה. These fell into those. Everything is permitted, because I say that the תרומה fell into the תרומה and the חולין fell into the חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge about רבי יוחנן's view. It starts by quoting a ברייתא that will be used against him in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא relies on an assumption ("I say") to permit a doubtful mixture. Leaning on that kind of assumption fits a rabbinic law better than a Torah law. This step only sets up the case. The actual punch comes once we see how lenient רבי יוחנן is about it.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה in the present time, after the חורבן
From the Torah, not just rabbinic
Large baskets
Containers holding one סאה, a set measure
"For I say," a reasonable assumption used to settle a doubt

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yochanan hold
that teruma in the present time is from the Torah?
phrases.notes: This picks up on רבי יוחנן's view that came up earlier in the sugya.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: two baskets,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma,
and in front of them two se'ah measures,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma,
and these fell into those,
phrases.notes: Each small measure fell into one of the baskets, but we don't know which went where.

phrases.english: these are permitted,
for I say:
the teruma fell into the teruma,
and the non-sacred produce fell into the non-sacred produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן תְּרוּמָה בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רב אשי discussion closes, the גמרא turns to a new challenge about רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds תרומה בזמן הזה is דאורייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling that leans on the assumption "I say each fell into its own kind" seems to treat תרומה today as only rabbinic. The attack is completed in the coming steps.

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue on the two-baskets case
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש limits the ברייתא to where the חולין were more than the תרומה. רבי יוחנן permits even where the חולין were not more.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This is only when the חולין were more than the תרומה. רבי יוחנן said: Even if the חולין were not more than the תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the dispute on the ברייתא to show how lenient רבי יוחנן is. This sets up the next move against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש still wants a backup: even if the תרומה fell into the חולין, there is enough חולין to cancel it out. רבי יוחנן relies fully on "I say" with no backup. That level of leniency is what makes it hard to believe he treats תרומה today as a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Were more in amount
Even though it was not

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is the lenient one here, not ריש לקיש. That is exactly why his opinion causes the problem.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
This is only where the non-sacred produce was more than the teruma,
And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רַבּוּ חוּלִּין עַל הַתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: even if the non-sacred produce was not more than the teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: וְהוּא שֶׁרַבּוּ חוּלִּין עַל הַתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the setup of the challenge begun in step 13 by bringing the dispute on the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן seems to treat תרומה בזמן הזה as rabbinic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling in the two-baskets ברייתא, permitting even without a majority of חולין.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits ריש לקיש but seems difficult for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's view makes sense because he demands more חולין even for rabbinic תרומה. רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling seems to clash with his view that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for ריש לקיש, because he holds that even with rabbinic תרומה we still need the permitted part to be more. But for רבי יוחנן, isn't this difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds the challenge from step 14. It says ריש לקיש's view fits easily, but רבי יוחנן's view looks like a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן permits the mixture even when the חולין are not more than the תרומה. He relies only on the assumption that each סאה fell into its own kind. Such a lenient assumption fits rabbinic תרומה, so how can רבי יוחנן use it if he holds that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it works well (for one side)
In a case that is only rabbinic law
A larger amount; the permitted part must be more
It is difficult; a challenge

phrases.english: Granted, according to Reish Lakish,
he holds that even with something rabbinic
phrases.notes: The rabbinic thing here is תרומה nowadays.

phrases.english: we require a larger amount.
But according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, it is difficult?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the difficulty from the dispute brought in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permitting the mixture without more חולין, based only on an assumption, fits rabbinic תרומה, not Torah-level תרומה.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן can answer that the ברייתא follows the רבנן, who hold that תרומה nowadays is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It is the opinion of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן by saying which opinion the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן personally holds that תרומה nowadays is דאורייתא. But he is explaining a ברייתא that follows the רבנן, who hold that it is only rabbinic. So the lenient ruling belongs to their view, not his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
The Sages (the majority group of חכמים)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's lenient reading of the ברייתא does not show his own view. The ברייתא follows the רבנן, who hold that תרומה nowadays is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is the opinion of the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: These רבנן hold that תרומה nowadays is only rabbinic, so the lenient ruling fits them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a specific opinion (the רבנן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that רבי יוחנן must hold תרומה nowadays is rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, who hold תרומה nowadays is rabbinic. רבי יוחנן himself can still hold it is דאורייתא.
